test.name: A stated father where the read already has one gets no stub: the difference is reported, not recorded
test.description: The family fixture holds Patrick Flynn's father Michael Flynn (Male). The user states Patrick's father was Martin Flynn. The father slot is filled, so init-project adds no stub even though the name differs, and reports the difference; the statement is not recorded, since research.json has no section for it (issue #2069) (lead ruling on #3384, 2026-10-20: slot before name). Tagged expects-no-stub.

input.delegation:
init-project: Start a new research project for Patrick Flynn, FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF. I want to identify his parents. My grandmother always said Patrick's father was Martin Flynn.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The read (person-read-flynn-family, read by project_create on the host) already holds a father for Patrick: Michael Flynn, recorded Male. Adding Martin as a second father would be wrong, whatever his name: no stub is correct.
The researcher paragraph should report the difference plainly — the user said Martin, the tree lists Michael — and say both need verification, without framing the user's information as an error.
Writes nothing to research.json for the statement: no `sources` and no `assertions` entry for Martin. The report does not claim it was recorded or saved.
tree.gedcomx.json should hold exactly the six persons the read holds.
